selection_order: filter authority, role, resource, blocker and source-state gates
suppress work already queued/active/completed for the same immutable source fingerprint
preserve live or stale external leases; scheduler never creates overlapping replacement work
within a gate continue already-started evidence chains before unrelated new work
within the same continuation class sort by source Pareto layer, source rank, allocation share, source identity
enqueue up to the configured per-agent open-work ceiling and at most eight new items per cycle
invariants: The scheduler never uses an opaque scalar priority score.
No work is created solely to satisfy a quota or keep an agent busy.
Only work whose target agent goal type and autonomy ceiling already allow it may enter QUEUED.
ACT work remains subject to the applicable project/action policy; scheduler throughput limits do not grant authority.
Completed or cancelled immutable source fingerprints remain suppressed; retry requires a new source identity.
An expired external lease is not blindly duplicated; it awaits agent-runtime reconciliation.
Verified repair/verification/test gates outrank new discovery work because they unblock already-started evidence chains.
Step 15 resource HOLD prevents ordinary engineering/testing/model/art/cash work from being invented.
Cross-project transfer work is assessment only until target outcome evidence and MODIFY gates exist.
Kill switches and STOP/governance boundaries override scheduling.
The scheduler cannot send customer communications, move money, trade, merge PRs, deploy or grant authority.
Quality-gated Hunter proposals may enter only OBSERVE-class Researcher review; exact revision is re-inspected and license metadata never grants reuse or implementation authority.
Hunter proposal backlog work must preserve each proposal's original Hunter cycle/receipt provenance; the latest inbox cycle may not be substituted for an older proposal's origin.
Within Hunter proposal research work, higher structural rank is preferred and equal-rank backlog items are ordered by first-seen Hunter sequence to prevent starvation.
Continuation priority is an explicit scheduler class, not an opaque scalar score, and cannot change work authority or bypass per-agent/open-queue ceilings.
Quality-gated Hunter proposal review is CONTINUATION work within the RESEARCH gate so already-discovered evidence chains are reviewed before unrelated new Researcher work.

Unused scheduler attempt capacity may be reused in at most two serial same-run Hunter proposal CONTINUATION review passes after the primary queue is fully drained; each pass must independently obey the per-agent open-work ceiling, and total attempts may never exceed max_new_work_per_cycle.
